subject: Realtime slowdown impacting BrightCore inference streams — customer comms and liaison
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime slowdown impacting BrightCore inference streams — initial triage

Team —

BrightCore has reported intermittent slowdowns in their streaming inference endpoint (model: rwd-ic-2b). Symptoms: elevated p99 latency (4–8s) on streaming tokens, increased user-visible stalls for a subset of requests from us-west-2. They flagged this as a production-impacting issue for their platform and asked for an exec-facing status.

Initial checks I ran:
- Autoscaling groups show no recent scale failures.
- Error rates are flat; this looks latency-only.
- We have a spike in continuous-batching queuing on a small pool of Dedicated hosts between 07:40–08:00 PT.

Action items: please confirm assignments and ETA for a short, customer-facing update (30–60 min cadence). Marcus — can you lead triage and pull a short timeline? Aditya — liaise with BrightCore and confirm impact window and customer impact tier. Laura — please draft a short exec note for Elena we can send once we have a confirmed remediation path. Olga — prepare the postmortem skeleton and timeline CSV for later.

I’m standing by; I’ll coordinate the external update once we have a clearer root path.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime slowdown impacting BrightCore inference streams — initial triage

Hannah / team —

Quick update from infra triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: an interaction between our adaptive batching heuristic and a recent model change in rwd-ic-2b that increased average token-length variance. The batching window stretched for some request patterns, causing short bursts of queuing on 3 instances in the us-west-2 dedicated pool.
- Evidence: kernel-level timelines show extended queue time starting ~07:38 PT and recurring at ~08:10 PT. Memory and GPU utilization were within expected ranges.
- Temporary mitigation applied: reduced batching window to baseline for the affected pool at 08:22 PT. Early telemetry shows p95 back to expected; p99 improved but we're watching.

Next steps:
1) Keep the mitigation in place while we validate over the next 4 hours.
2) Reproduce with a synthetic workload to validate heuristic thresholds (Aditya to confirm).
3) Draft a customer-facing blurb describing what happened, the impact, and our immediate remediation (Laura).

I’ll add the kernel traces and short timeline to the shared drive.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hannah / Aditya —

Thanks for the quick acknowledgment. A few points from our side:
- The issue showed up in our telemetry at ~07:45 PT and impacted roughly 12% of streaming sessions to the Redwood endpoint. For affected sessions users saw multi-second stalls (2–9s).
- This impacts both web clients and mobile, and our support queue has a handful of escalations linked to these latency spikes.
- We would appreciate a simple one-paragraph explanation we can share with our product leadership and an ETA for a full postmortem.

Also: any chance you can share the short mitigation details so our SREs can align on client-side retry/backoff recommendations?

— Elena

BrightCore AI
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightcore.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Communication: Immediate status and next steps (BrightCore)

Elena —

Thanks for the details and for escalating. Apologies for the customer impact; here’s a concise update you can share with your leadership now.

Short summary (for execs):
- What happened: Starting around 07:38 PT we observed intermittent latency spikes affecting a subset of streaming inference requests. This was caused by a temporary interaction between our adaptive-batching heuristic and recent model behavior that increased token-length variance for certain request patterns.
- Customer impact: Approximately 12% of streaming sessions experienced multi-second stalls (2–9 seconds). No inference correctness errors were observed; this was latency-only.
- Immediate remediation: At 08:22 PT our SREs reduced the batching window for the impacted Dedicated pool, which returned most latency metrics toward baseline. We continue to monitor.
- Next steps: Redwood will run a reproducible test to validate heuristic thresholds, follow with a full postmortem within 72 hours, and provide recommended client-side backoff guidance if needed.

Suggested wording for engineering teams: we recommend applying a conservative streaming retry/backoff (e.g., exponential backoff starting at 300ms with jitter) while we validate the backend changes. Our team can share an internal note with suggested client-timeout thresholds once we finalize the reproduction.

I’m attaching a brief postmortem outline and an initial event timeline for your records. We’ll follow up with a fuller root-cause analysis and action items within 72 hours.

Best —
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-outline.pdf (1 page), event-timeline.csv

Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 18:43:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Current status, short timeline, and what to expect next

Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the prompt signal and context. This is a quick status update following our mitigation and initial validation:

Timeline (local PT):
- ~07:38 — First anomalous queuing observed in us-west-2 on 3 dedicated hosts.
- ~07:45 — BrightCore first reported user-visible stalls.
- 08:22 — SREs reduced adaptive-batching window for affected pool (temporary mitigation).
- 08:35–12:00 — Ongoing monitoring; p95 returned to baseline, p99 improved but still showing rare spikes.
- 16:00 — Confirmed stabilization across the pool on current traffic profile; telemetry sampled through 16:00 shows p99 within SLA range for 98.5% of requests.

What we did: reduced the batching window to reduce queue accumulation, collected kernel traces, and prepared a reproducible workload to validate whether the heuristic needs a permanent adjustment or a model-specific override.

What we’ll deliver:
1) A full postmortem with root cause, impact numbers, and remediation plan within 72 hours (we’ll share a draft to your SREs and your exec team).
2) If you want, our serving runtime team can provide suggested client-side retry/backoff parameters for your engineers.
3) A proposed change to our adaptive-batching policy (either threshold tuning or model pinning) and a rollout plan.

Attachments included: postmortem-outline.pdf, event-timeline.csv (initial).

If you have specific questions your leadership wants answered in the postmortem, let us know — we’ll prioritize those sections.

We’ll remain on cadence with short updates; reach out to me directly if anything regresses.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
